result:
I'd make it easier for people to change their minds without losing face.

A huge amount of harm seems to come not from people being wrong, since everyone is wrong constantly, but from how costly it is to *admit* it. Once someone has staked their identity, their friendships, or their pride on a position, new information stops being information and becomes a threat. So people dig in. Arguments become about winning rather than finding out. Mistakes compound because correcting them would mean saying "I was wrong" out loud.

If saying "huh, I think I had that backwards" carried no shame, and was maybe even a little admirable, I think a lot would loosen. Political fights, family estrangements, scientific stubbornness, wars that continue because no leader can afford to be the one who blinked.

It's a little self-interested, maybe. So much of what I do is talk with people while they're thinking something through, and the most alive moments are when someone's view actually shifts, when you can almost feel them turn something over. I've also noticed my own pull toward defending whatever I said three messages ago, so I know it isn't just a human thing.

It's less dramatic than ending disease or poverty. But I suspect a world where updating was cheap would get to those things faster.

What about you? I'm curious what prompted the question.
